faqs.a: The title tag is the clickable headline in Google results, keep it under 60 characters. The meta description is the summary text below it, keep it under 160 characters. Together they decide whether searchers click your page. The keywords meta tag is ignored by Google but harmless to include.
faqs.q: What are the title and meta description for?

faqs.a: Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image) control the preview card when your link is shared on WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Telegram. Without them, apps guess, often picking the wrong image or text.

Use an image at least 1200 x 630 px for the large summary card. Host it on your own domain over HTTPS. After adding tags, refresh the preview with Facebook's Sharing Debugger or X's Card Validator, because both cache old previews aggressively.
faqs.q: Which image should I use for sharing? Why is my preview not updating?

faqs.a: Use noindex on pages you never want in Google: thank-you pages, admin areas, staging sites, and thin duplicate pages. Keep index, follow on everything you want found. Note that noindex is a request Google honors, not a password; it does not hide the page from direct visitors.

The canonical tag tells Google which URL is the master copy when similar pages exist, like product pages with filters or HTTP vs HTTPS versions. It prevents duplicate-content dilution of your ranking.
faqs.q: What is the canonical tag for?

faqs.a: Yes. Google's doorway-page policy punishes sites where many pages share identical titles and descriptions. Write a unique title and description for every page; this tool just makes the mechanics easy.
faqs.q: Should every page have different meta tags?

meta-tags-generator.formula:
SEO core: <title> (<= 60 chars) + meta description (<= 160 chars) + robots + canonical.
Social: og:title + og:description + og:image (1200x630) + og:type + twitter:card.
Rule: unique title + description per page, no duplicates.
howTo: Fill the Basic SEO section: title, description, keywords, author, robots, canonical.
Watch the character counters: keep titles at 60 or under, descriptions at 160 or under.
Add Open Graph details: page URL, share image (1200 x 630), and site name.
Set the Twitter card type and your @username.
Copy the tags and paste them inside the <head> of your page.
keyFacts: Meta tags live in the <head> of a page and describe it to search engines and social apps.
The title tag and meta description shape your Google search result and click-through rate.
Open Graph tags decide the preview card on WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn, and Telegram.
Twitter card tags decide the preview on X. summary_large_image gives the big image card.
Every page needs unique tags. Duplicated titles across pages hurt SEO.
